text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Monday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- Supporters of the ruling Socialist Party of Serbia (SPS) will hold a final rally in Belgrade on Tuesday December 24 at noon. People to be bussed in from all over the country.
- Supporters of opposition coalition Zajedno and students continue their protests over annullment of election results.
- The independent union of farmers of Serbia announced it would block roads in Serbia on Monday demanding payment of products delivered to factories.
- Twenty six more department stores of the Company of Department Stores - Belgrade join a strike started by two stores on December 18. The company has a total of 43 stores throughout Yugoslavia.
- Samoborcek from Samobor and Putnik from Belgrade to start operating a regular bus line Belgrade-Zagreb via the highway from Tuesday December 23.

- The stability of the domestic currency and continued growth of the GDP are among positive results of 1996 year while slow implementation of ownership transformation is negative, says director of Econmics institute Danko Djunic.
- There is no reason for refugees to join the protests of opposition coalition Zajedno, says president of the committee for protection of refugee rights Borislav Mikelic.
- Montenegrin parliament continues session Monday, its agenda includes election of new government.
